title: rclone mount leads to DELETE when appending to a remotely locked file
body:
#### What is the problem you are having with rclone?
I've noticed that when I write (append) to a file over rclone mount in quick succession, sometimes ownCloud returns a 423 (file locked). This results in rclone giving a DELETE on the file.

#### What is your rclone version (output from `rclone version`)
rclone --version
rclone v1.47.0
- os/arch: linux/amd64
- go version: go1.11.5

#### Which OS you are using and how many bits (eg Windows 7, 64 bit)
CentOS Linux release 7.6 (64 bit)

####  Which cloud storage system are you using? (eg Google Drive)
ownCloud (10.0.10 and 10.1)


#### The command you were trying to run (eg `rclone copy /tmp remote:tmp`)
Mounting:
```
rclone mount -vvv --debug-fuse --vfs-cache-mode=full owncloud:/ /mnt/rclone/ 2>&1|tee /tmrclone_append-full-surfdrive.log
```

Then I run:
```
time for i in {1..100}
do 
    echo run $i >> /mnt/rclone/rclone_appending.txt
done
```
This works for a time, but after a while it will start erroring:
```
-bash: echo: write error: Input/output error
```

#### A log from the command with the `-vv` flag (eg output from `rclone -vv copy /tmp remote:tmp`)

Apache logs:

So what seems to be happening, is that every append leads to a PUT and a PROPFIND. Then, apparently, once every so often ownCloud is not done yet with releasing the file lock, and returns a 423. And what happens next is that rclone gives a DELETE. Now the file is gone, locally and remotely. In ownCloud, you can see the file in the trashbin, and restore it from there. But locally the file stays gone, and both rclone and my loop are unable to write to it.
